key_insight: CORTEX adds structured, step-by-step reasoning traces to 3D chest CT QA so MLLMs can show how they reach an answer, not just the final prediction.
clinical_relevance: This could make chest CT AI outputs more interpretable and easier for radiologists to verify against scan evidence.
method: Built a benchmark on CT-RATE with four diagnostic stages: task understanding, visual observation, diagnostic reasoning, and answer synthesis.
Generated reasoning traces with frontier LLMs and filtered them using automated rubric scoring plus expert radiologist review.
Covers open-ended VQA, closed-ended VQA, and report generation for 3D chest CT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 76,177 validated reasoning traces with stage-level evaluation designed collaboratively with clinicians.
watch_item: The benchmark improves supervision and evaluation, but real-world usefulness will still depend on whether models can generalize these structured traces reliably across diverse scanners, protocols, and cases.
paper_title: CORTEX: A Structured Reasoning Benchmark for Trustworthy 3D Chest CT MLLMs
